dataset: SARS-CoV-2 reference plus three variant genomes, aligned with MAFFT

accessions.why: Complete 29,738 bp genome with 11 gene and 12 CDS features and no ambiguity codes anywhere, spike included. The lineage is stated in the record's reference title ('The Alpha variant (B.1.1.7) of SARS-CoV-2...'). A human isolate submitted without any claim of rights.

Complete 29,689 bp genome with 11 gene and 12 CDS features and no ambiguity codes anywhere, spike included. The lineage is explicit in the record as /note="genotype: B.1.617.2", which is stronger evidence than a study title. A human isolate submitted without any claim of rights.

Complete 29,738 bp genome with 11 gene and 12 CDS features and no ambiguity codes anywhere, spike included; the lineage is explicit as /note="genotype: BA.1.1". Chosen over a record designated plain BA.1 because every bare-BA.1 candidate carried at least one ambiguity code, while this BA.1 sublineage is ambiguity-free. Engineered constructs (for example reporter clones carrying nLuc) were excluded; this is a natural human isolate submitted without any claim of rights.

reference.note: The bundled RefSeq reference, unchanged by this script.

source.note: No GISAID data: GISAID's terms forbid redistribution.

mafft.note: MAFFT's stdout is written unedited; --preservecase keeps the uppercase residues extracted from the GenBank records, and --auto picks MAFFT's default strategy.

licence.statement: NCBI places no restrictions on the use or distribution of GenBank data, but notes that some submitters may claim patent, copyright or other rights. Each record above was checked for such a claim and none was found.
